plugins.summary: Layer clouds like the suyari-gasumi bands of yamato-e and Rinpa across the upper to middle canvas as long horizontal bands. Each band is a long outline with rounded ends in thin pale-ink (gray) brush, with one bleeding thick-brush gold (yellow) line through its core. The bands overlap downward, shifted left and right, the lower ones shorter and narrower. The written band count (1–5), or 3–4 when none is written. The left-right direction and the height of the bands come from four arrangements.

Shade the sky down from the top edge like the ichimonji bokashi of ukiyo-e and nihonga. Bleeding strokes the full width are laid from the top down: close together and dark at the top (thick-brush ultramarine), opening out lower down and fading from thin-brush ultramarine to pale ink (gray); the lowest three are a little shorter. The written stroke count (1–12), or 8–10 when none is written, drawn from the top down.

Let rain fall over the whole canvas like Hiroshige's sudden shower. The rain is thin vertical pen lines: pale-ink (gray) lines 0.38 long scattered over the canvas, with 12 somewhat longer ultramarine lines scattered among them. The written rain count (the pale-ink lines, 1–80), or 36–48 when none is written; the 12 ultramarine lines are always drawn.

Scatter snow over the whole canvas like gofun peony snow. The flakes are bleeding white points: the written number of small flakes, 14 middle ones and 6 large peony flakes. Being white, they belong on a dark ground such as ink wash, charcoal, blue or black. The written flake count (the small flakes, 1–80), or 36–48 when none is written.
